The farmhouse was in a poor condition. There was nothing but burnt-yellow grass with bushes everywhere. The tall dense trees had wilted. This happened because the gardener who used to take care of the garden had passed away due to illness, and the grandparents were not able to pay as much attention as required.

The writer decided to bring the same scenery back with the help of his father, sister and brothers. His elder brothers took charge of bringing fertiliser from the market and planting new plants. His sister opted to water plants in the afternoon, and the writer had the responsibility of taking care of the nests. They started working with full energy and got everything back to the way it used to be within a month's time.

You can restore a garden by planting new plants, watering them regularly, removing bushes and weeds, and taking care of the trees and nests with the help of your family.

The writer was shocked and sad when he saw the burnt grass and wilted trees. He murmured: Oh my God! What happened to them?

We can keep ourselves safe from Covid-19 by washing our hands with soap, wearing a mask, maintaining physical distance, and covering our face while sneezing.

lessons.title: The Lesson: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Fable: 'What Goes Around, Comes Around'

The frog tied the mouse's foot to his own with a piece of thread so that he could pull the mouse along to see the wonderful underwater world, because the mouse could not swim. The frog laughed as he thought it would be good fun for him.

The poor mouse was drowned, while the cruel frog frisked about down below, tied to the foot of the mouse. Just then, a hawk saw the mouse and pounced upon it. As he flew away with it, the frog was dragged out of the water too, for he was still tied to the mouse. The hawk said he wanted them both and would eat the frog first, for he liked frog meat even better than mouse meat. In a few moments, the hawk had a good supper, and there was nothing left of either the selfish frog or the poor mouse.

A mouse who lived on land met a frog who lived in water. The frog tied the mouse's foot to his own with a thread to show him the underwater world. The frog jumped into the pond and swam happily, but the poor mouse drowned. A hawk pounced on the mouse and dragged the frog out too, and ate them both. Moral: As you sow, so shall you reap.

My favourite character is the mouse, because he was innocent and trusted his friend, even though the frog deceived him.

The Hare and the Tortoise

Once there lived a hare and a tortoise in a forest. The hare was very proud of his speed. He used to make fun of the tortoise for being too slow. One day, the tortoise challenged the hare to a race. The hare accepted the challenge. The race started. The hare ran very fast. The tortoise was left much behind. The hare got tired and stopped to have some rest under a tree. He fell asleep. The tortoise passed by him and reached the winning post. The hare woke up and ran as fast as he could. He saw that the tortoise was already there at the winning post. The tortoise had won the race.

lessons.title: The Lesson: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Poem: 'A Nation's Strength'

A nation's strength is not gold but men. Brave men who work while others sleep, who dare while others fly, who stand fast for truth and honour's sake and suffer long — they build a nation's pillars deep and lift them to the sky.

The message of the poem is that good people are more important than gold and jewels. A nation becomes great and strong through brave, truthful and hardworking people who serve it selflessly.

Education is important because it makes a nation strong by making people learned and skillful. It also makes lives better for those who need to struggle for their survival. Strong nations always work hard for the welfare of society.

We can contribute by being truthful, brave and hardworking, by getting education, by obeying the law, and by working for the welfare of society.

The main idea of the poem is that the secret of a nation's success is its manpower. Good people are more important than gold and jewels. If a nation has brave and selfless people who fight for truth and honour, no one can stop it from making progress and getting strong.

Markhors eat grass in spring and summer, but they feed on leaves, herbs, fruits and flowers in winter.

The long and curly horns on males are nearly 63 inches long, and on females around 10 inches long.

A markhor has a lifespan of 12 to 13 years.

Markhors are endangered because they are killed by hunters particularly for their meat and horns. Their horns are used for traditional medicines and trophies.

Markhor is the national animal of Pakistan. It belongs to the goat family and is one of the most beautiful wild animals of Pakistan. It is considered a symbol of bravery and intelligence. It can jump downwards from mountain peaks with ease, and can also kill snakes. It is known for its long and curly horns. Its strong, powerful legs give it the ability to maintain balance when climbing. It has extremely keen senses of sight and smell, and it grazes mostly on the peaks of mountains so it is out of the range of predators.

lessons.notes_html:
Poem: 'Two Little Kittens'

The kittens began to quarrel because one had a mouse and the other had none, and that was the way the quarrel begun.

The old woman swept the kittens out of the room because they began to quarrel and then to fight.

The kittens learnt that fighting is a bad thing. They found it much better to lie by the fire than to quarrel and fight.

Fighting is a bad thing because when we fight with others we often harm ourselves too. The kittens were swept out of the room into the storm and came back wet with snow and as cold as ice. So we should always avoid fighting.

The setting of the poem is a house on a stormy night. The words that helped are: 'One stormy night', 'wet with snow', 'as cold as ice', and 'lie by the fire'.

Fighting is a bad thing because it harms us and others, breaks friendships, and makes us sad. Peace and kindness are better than quarrelling.

The moral of the poem is that fighting is a bad thing, so always try to avoid it. We know this because the kittens realised their mistake and found it much better to lie by the fire than to quarrel and fight.

This poem is about two little kittens. They began to quarrel with each other during a stormy night. One kitten had a mouse but the other kitten had none, so their quarrel began. The old woman became angry and swept them out of her house with her broom. Then, they returned wet and cold. They realised their mistake and felt ashamed. They found that it is better to lie by the fire in the house than to quarrel and fight. They had learnt that fighting is a bad thing, so always try to avoid it.
